title: Tategaki
description: Vertical Japanese text, set properly: shuhari — obey the form, break the form, leave the form — as an editorial monument.
usage: Tategaki is not rotated text: writing-mode vertical-rl lays the columns right-to-left with the glyphs upright, the way a book opens. The three characters are shuhari (守破離), the craft discipline this whole library runs on — first obey the mold, then break it deliberately, then leave it behind. Use the part for chapter heads, manifestos, and the page that states what a studio believes.
a11y: Vertical text is genuinely harder for some readers, so the part always travels with its horizontal gloss: the three terms, translated, in reading order beside it. Screen readers receive the text in DOM order — characters, then gloss — regardless of the visual direction.
